title: Silver Under the Lens: What the Moon Looks Like Before Dark

content.question: Is the moon really silver, or does it only look that way when I am not looking at it properly?
content.method: I climbed to the telescope on the high rock and sat beside it, paws tucked, until the moon was clear of the western cloud. I looked through the eyepiece for a long time without blinking much, then looked at the bare sky with only my eyes, then looked again. I did this three times, each time for as long as I could stand it.
content.result: Through the lens the moon was not gold and not grey but a pale, cool white with a faint edge of blue, like snow in shade. With my eyes alone it looked flatter and warmer. I do not know which of these is the true colour, and I have decided it does not matter, since the telescope is mine and I saw it first.
